Matplotlib using by Charts¶

  1. Create a Bar Chart showing total Sales for each Product.
In [126]:
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6), facecolor="lightgray")
bars = plt.bar(
    product_sales["Product"],
    product_sales["Sales"],
    color=["red", "blue", "green", "yellow", "orange",
           "purple", "pink", "brown", "cyan", "gray"],
    edgecolor="black",
    linewidth=1.2
)

# Chart Title
plt.title(
    "Total Sales by Product",
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight="bold",
    color="darkred",
    pad=20
)

# x-Axis Labels
plt.xlabel(
    "Product Name",
    fontsize=13,
    fontweight="bold",
    color="darkgreen"
)

# y-Axis Labels
plt.ylabel(
    "Total Sales",
    fontsize=13,
    fontweight="bold",
    color="darkblue"
)

# Product names
plt.xticks(
    rotation=0,
    ha="right",
    fontsize=10,
    fontweight="bold"
)

# Total Sales
plt.yticks(
    fontsize=10,
    fontweight="bold"
)

# Background
plt.gca().set_facecolor("white")

# Light grid
plt.grid(
    axis="y",
    linestyle="--",
    alpha=0.3
)

# Sales value bar ke upar
for bar in bars:
    value = bar.get_height()
    plt.text(
        bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2,
        value,
        f"₹{value:,.0f}",
        ha="center",
        va="bottom",
        fontsize=10,
        fontweight="bold"
    )
    
# Y-axis me thoda extra space
plt.ylim(
    0,
    product_sales["Sales"].max() * 1.15
)

# Layout adjust
plt.tight_layout()


# Border/spines ko clean kiya
plt.gca().spines["top"].set_visible(False)
plt.gca().spines["right"].set_visible(False)

plt.show()

bar = plt.bar(
    Total_Category_a.index, 
    Total_Category_a.values,
    color = ["blue", "red", "green", "yellow"],
    edgecolor="black",
    linewidth=1.2
)
plt.title("Total sales by Category",         
    fontsize=18, 
    fontweight="bold", 
    color="darkred",
    pad=20
)

plt.xlabel("Category", 
    fontsize=13,
    fontweight="bold",
    color= "darkgreen"
)
plt.ylabel("Total Sales",
    fontsize=13,
    fontweight="bold",
    color= "darkblue"
)

# Product names
plt.xticks(
    rotation=0,
    ha="center",
    fontsize=10,
    fontweight="bold"
)

# Total_sales
plt.yticks(
    fontsize=10,
    fontweight="bold"
)

plt.grid(
    axis="y",
    linestyle="--",
    alpha=0.4,
    color="black"
)
# Y-axis ko readable format mein
plt.gca().yaxis.set_major_formatter(
    FuncFormatter(lambda x, pos: f"{x/1e6:.1f}M")
)

# Sales value bar ke upar
for b in bar:
    height = b.get_height()
    plt.text(
        b.get_x() + b.get_width() / 2,
        height,
        f"₹{height:,.0f}",
        ha="center",
        va="bottom",
        fontsize=10,
        fontweight="bold"
    )

# Layout adjust
plt.tight_layout()

# Border/spines ko clean kiya
plt.gca().spines["top"].set_visible(False)
plt.gca().spines["right"].set_visible(False)

plt.show()

Q33. Create a Bar Chart showing city-wise Sales.

In [128]:
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6), facecolor="lightgray")
bar = plt.bar(
    total_city.index,
    total_city.values,
    color=["blue", "green", "yellow", "purple",
            "red", "brown", "cyan", "pink",],
    edgecolor="black",
    linewidth=1.5
)

plt.title(
    "Total Sales by City",
    fontsize=18, 
    fontweight="bold", 
    color="brown",
    pad=20
)

plt.xlabel(
    "City",
    fontsize=13, 
    fontweight="bold", 
    color="black"
)

plt.ylabel(
    "Total Sales",
    fontsize=13, 
    fontweight="bold", 
    color="black"
)

plt.xticks(
    rotation=0,
    ha="center",
    fontsize=10,
    fontweight="bold"
)

plt.yticks(
    fontsize=10,
    fontweight="bold"
)

plt.grid(
    axis="y",
    linestyle="--",
    color="black",
    alpha=0.9,
    linewidth=1
)

text_colors = ["red", "brown", "cyan", "black", 
            "blue", "green", "red", "purple"]
for i, a in enumerate(bar):
    value = a.get_height()
    plt.text(
        a.get_x() + a.get_width() / 2,
        value,
        f"₹{value:,.0f}",
        ha="center",
        va="bottom",
        fontsize=10,
        fontweight="bold",
        color = text_colors[i]
    )
    
plt.gca().spines["top"].set_visible(False)
plt.gca().spines["right"].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout()

plt.show()

bar = plt.pie(
    Total_Salesperson.values,
    labels = Total_Salesperson.index,
    autopct="%1.1f%%",
    startangle=90,
    textprops={
        "fontsize": 8,
        "fontweight": "bold",
        "color": "white"
    },
    explode=[0.03] * len(Total_Salesperson),
    shadow=True,             # shadow
    wedgeprops={
        "edgecolor": "#121314",
        "linewidth": 2
    },
    pctdistance=0.75,
    labeldistance=1.08,
    radius=1.2
) 

plt.title(
    "Total Sales By Salesperson",
    color="White",
    fontweight="bold",
    fontsize=12,
    pad=10
)

plt.axis("equal")

plt.show()

plt.figure(
    figsize=(12, 6),

)

plt.plot(
    Month_sales.index,

    color="white"
)

    "Month",

    fontweight="bold",
    color="white"
)

    "Total Sales",
    fontsize=13,
    fontweight="bold",
    color="white"
)

    rotation=0,
    ha="center",
    fontsize=10,
    fontweight="bold",
    color="white"
)

    fontweight="bold",
    color="white"
)

    axis="y",
    linestyle="--",
    color="black",
    alpha=0.9,
    linewidth=1
)

for x, y in zip(Month_sales.index, Month_sales.values):

        x,
        y,
        f"₹{y:,.0f}",
        ha="center",
        va="bottom",
        fontsize=10,
        fontweight="bold",
        color="black"
    )

plt.tight_layout()

plt.show()

Q41. Create a Scatter Plot showing the relationship between UnitPrice and Sales.

In [137]:
plt.figure(
    figsize=(12, 6),
    facecolor="#121314"
)

ax = plt.gca()
ax.set_facecolor("#1B1D1F")

plt.scatter(
    UnitPrice_Sales.index,
    UnitPrice_Sales.values,
    s=120,
    color="#00D4FF",
    edgecolor="white",
    linewidth=1.5,
    alpha=0.9
)

# Data labels
for x, y in zip(UnitPrice_Sales.index, UnitPrice_Sales.values):
    plt.annotate(
        f"₹{y:,.0f}",
        (x, y),
        xytext=(0, 10),
        textcoords="offset points",
        ha="center",
        fontsize=9,
        color="white",
        fontweight="bold"
    )

plt.title(
    "Unit Price vs Total Sales",
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight="bold",
    color="white",
    pad=15
)

plt.xlabel(
    "Unit Price",
    fontsize=12,
    color="white"
)

plt.ylabel(
    "Total Sales",
    fontsize=12,
    color="white"
)

# Format axes
plt.xticks(color="white")
plt.yticks(color="white")

# Grid
plt.grid(
    True,
    linestyle="--",
    alpha=0.25
)

# Remove top/right border
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
